question:
A previously healthy 23-year-old male college student is brought to the emergency department by EMS
after his roommate called for help. The patient presents with severe headache and fever that began 6
hours ago. On examination, his vital signs show: temperature 39.5°C, heart rate 120/min, and blood
pressure 83/68 mm Hg. Physical findings include a generalized petechial rash on his extremities and
trunk, and marked nuchal rigidity. He is oriented to person and place, demonstrates purposeful
movement of all extremities, has normal pupillary and corneal reflexes bilaterally, an intact cough
reflex, and no focal neurological deficits. The patient's Covid-19 vaccinations are current, and
SARS-CoV-2 testing is negative. He has received 2 liters of intravenous fluid. What is the correct
sequence of steps for initial evaluation and treatment of this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Brain
imaging, lumbar puncture, then administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone (B) Blood culture,
administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone, then lumbar puncture (C) Blood culture, brain
imaging, then administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone (D) Lumbar puncture, administration of
antibiotics and dexamethasone, then blood culture (E) Brain imaging, blood culture, then administration
of antibiotics and dexamethasone (F) Lumbar puncture, blood culture, then administration of antibiotics
and dexamethasone (G) Administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone, blood culture, then lumbar
puncture (H) Administration of antibiotics, brain imaging, then lumbar puncture (I) Administration of
dexamethasone, blood culture, then lumbar puncture (J) Blood culture, lumbar puncture, then
administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone
 A. Brain imaging, blood culture, then administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone
B. Administration of dexamethasone, blood culture, then lumbar puncture
C. Blood culture, administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone, then lumbar puncture
D. Blood culture, brain imaging, then administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone
E. Administration of antibiotics, brain imaging, then lumbar puncture
F. Blood culture, lumbar puncture, then administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone
G. Lumbar puncture, administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone, then blood culture
H. Administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone, blood culture, then lumbar puncture
I. Lumbar puncture, blood culture, then administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone
J. Brain imaging, lumbar puncture, then administration of antibiotics and dexamethasone
